newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares pierce 18,000, seen up on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares pierce 18,000, seen up on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares pierced 18,000 points on Friday, setting a third straight 34-month high, and analysts said the stronger buying after price-fixing signalled the recent foreign buying frenzy would continue next week.
"It seems to me that next week can be very similar to this though for about two weeks there's been no fundamental reason for that to happen," said Tomasz Berent, an analyst at IB Austria Securities.
Some analysts said growth could slow next week with some investors taking profits. The market rose 4.1 percent this week and has risen 36.8 percent since mid-December.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose two percent to 18,177.2 points and turnover rose 19.8 percent to 260.9 million zlotys ($86.1) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 67 to 12 with nine stocks flat.

Builder Elektromontaz Export, confectionery Wedel, builder KPBP Bick, cable maker BFK and tyre maker Debica all rose by or near the daily maximum 10 percent, with the latter boosted by strong January earnings released on Thursday, analysts said.
They said investors would be watching January data to be released by the bulk of listed firms early next week.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 2.1 percent to 167 zlotys ($55.1) in regular bourse trade in a turnover of 27.4 million zlotys ($9 million).
In continuous trade the units fell 2.7 percent to 163.5 zlotys ($53.9) in a 27-million-zloty turnover ($8.9 million).
Live trade stock turnover was at 25.4 million zlotys ($8.4 million) with 16 issues down and five flat and the WIG 20 index down 0.7 percent to 1,870.2 points.
